title: He Was an Uncapped Walk-in Three Years Ago. On Sunday Rajat Patidar Leads RCB Into the IPL Final in Ahmedabad.
excerpt: The defending champions crushed Gujarat Titans by ninety-two runs in Qualifier 1. Now they wait for Friday's Qualifier 2 to learn whether Gujarat or Rajasthan will meet them at the Narendra Modi Stadium. No team has won back-to-back IPL titles since 2011.
body:
On Tuesday night in Dharamsala, Rajat Patidar stood at the crease with the Himalayas behind him and the IPL final ahead. He had been dropped on twenty. He finished on ninety-three off thirty-three balls, with five fours and nine sixes, posting the highest score by a captain in IPL playoff history. Royal Challengers Bengaluru crushed Gujarat Titans by ninety-two runs. The defending champions are back in the final.

They will play on Sunday, May 31, at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. Their opponent will be decided on Friday, when Gujarat Titans — bruised, humiliated, but not eliminated — face Rajasthan Royals in Qualifier 2. The winner goes to Ahmedabad. The loser goes home.

## The Making of a Captain

Three years ago, Rajat Patidar was an uncapped domestic cricketer from Indore. He had been bought by RCB for his base price, twenty lakh rupees, the kind of auction afterthought that teams forget by the third week of the tournament.

Then came the 2022 playoffs. Patidar walked into Qualifier 2 against Rajasthan Royals as an injury replacement, a man who had not been in the original squad. He scored an unbeaten century — 112 off 54 balls — the fastest hundred in IPL playoff history at the time. It remains one of the most remarkable individual performances in the tournament's eighteen-year existence.

RCB built their future around that innings. By 2025, Patidar was the vice-captain. By the final against Punjab Kings, he was the emotional centre of a team that had waited sixteen years for its first title. When RCB won, the franchise that had been cricket's most lovable chokers finally had a champion. When they needed a captain for 2026, there was never really a debate.

## What Awaits in Ahmedabad

RCB arrive at the Narendra Modi Stadium with five days of rest and a bowling attack that has been the best in the tournament. Jacob Duffy, the New Zealander who was an unknown quantity in March, has taken twenty-four wickets at an economy rate under seven. Mohammed Siraj, bowling with the confidence of a man who has finally settled into his skin, has been devastating with the new ball. Kagiso Rabada, now holding the all-time record for powerplay wickets in a single IPL season with eighteen, gives them the kind of three-pronged pace attack that most teams can only dream of.

Their batting is led by the inevitable Virat Kohli, who became the first player in IPL history to score six hundred runs in four consecutive seasons. Kohli, who has played more IPL matches than any human alive, is chasing something that has eluded even him — back-to-back titles.

No team has won consecutive IPL titles since Chennai Super Kings in 2010 and 2011. Mumbai Indians came close with their 2019 and 2020 wins, but the second of those came in the biosecure bubble of the UAE, a tournament so different from normal IPL cricket that many fans consider it an asterisk. If RCB win on Sunday, they will join an exclusive club.

## The Other Side

Gujarat Titans, who finished second in the league stage with eighteen points, face a brutal road. Their ninety-two-run loss to RCB in Qualifier 1 exposed batting frailties that head coach Ashish Nehra will need to address in forty-eight hours. Shubman Gill, their captain, has been inconsistent in the pressure moments. Jos Buttler, the Englishman who was supposed to anchor the middle order, has looked nothing like the player who once scored four centuries in a single IPL season.

Rajasthan Royals, however, are riding the wave of something that defies conventional cricket logic. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, their fifteen-year-old opener, has 583 runs, 53 sixes, and a strike rate of 232 this season. His 97 off 29 balls in the Eliminator against Sunrisers Hyderabad broke Chris Gayle's all-time record for sixes in a single IPL season. He is a child playing a game that grown men cannot.

If Rajasthan win Friday's Qualifier 2, the final becomes a story that writes itself: the defending champions and their experienced captain against the team with the youngest phenomenon the sport has ever produced.

## For NRIs Watching From Abroad

The IPL 2026 Final on Sunday, May 31 starts at 7:30 PM IST, which translates to 10:00 AM Eastern and 7:00 AM Pacific in the United States, 3:00 PM BST in the United Kingdom, and 10:00 AM EST in Toronto. JioHotstar streams every ball in India. In the US and UK, Willow TV and Sky Sports carry the broadcast respectively.

The Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad seats 132,000. It will be full. For NRIs who have followed this IPL season from thousands of miles away — through dawn alarms, muted office streams, and WhatsApp score updates — Sunday is the day the season comes down to forty overs and one question.

Can Rajat Patidar, the man nobody picked, lead the team nobody believed in to something nobody thought possible — back-to-back titles?
